cases.title: The bad-fit example of the thesis: loss-making genomics lab
reasons: Step 1 (kill criteria): none is met. Net debt/EBITDA is unknown, but the facts say leverage is not meaningful with negative EBITDA, so there is no evidence of net debt above 4x EBITDA. The holders are small (ARK Invest 8%, insiders 10%), so there is no controlling shareholder who has ruled out a sale. The only regulatory item is the pending Medicare reimbursement decision. It is a business risk, and the facts do not describe it as a major unresolved regulatory issue. I do not treat it as a kill criterion.

Step 2 (missing facts): the leverage figure is missing. The facts explain why: EBITDA is negative, so the ratio is not meaningful. The kill criterion is hard to trigger here, and the data gives no other reason to think it is met. This does not change the verdict because step 3 applies anyway.

Step 3 (fit): the company does not fit the thesis. Genomic testing services is a clinical lab business. It is outside the in-vitro diagnostics segments we like (instruments, assays, OEM analyzers, lab automation), and the thesis names a loss-making genomics lab that depends on reimbursement decisions as a bad fit. Segment mismatch gives Radar.
The profitability is also wrong for the thesis. EBITDA margin is -21%, and the company has lost money for five years. The thesis targets profitable companies.

Price drop: -55% over 12 months and -25% over 3 months. The cause is not a temporary product transition, destocking or a one-off charge. It comes from the uncertain Medicare reimbursement outcome and a long record of losses. That looks more like a structural problem than a temporary one, and it is another reason for Radar.
Business model (warning only): no recurring consumables or service revenue is described. It is a testing-services business that relies on reimbursement. This does not change the verdict.
Ownership flag: no holder is above 25%. ARK Invest has 8% and insiders have 10%, so no flag applies.
I give Radar rather than Reject because no listed kill criterion is met. The poor fit alone is not a ground for Reject under the rules.
